// Stands in for server/models.mjs during evaluation: the real local models, with text embeddings memoised.
import * as real from "../../server/models.mjs";
export * from "../../server/models.mjs"; // everything else unchanged (embedText below takes precedence)

const cache = new Map();
export const embedStats = { hits: 0, misses: 0, ms: 0 };

export async function embedText(text) {
  const key = String(text);
  const hit = cache.get(key);
  if (hit) {
    embedStats.hits++;
    return hit;
  }
  const t0 = performance.now();
  const v = await real.embedText(key);
  embedStats.ms += Math.round(performance.now() - t0);
  embedStats.misses++;
  cache.set(key, v);
  return v;
}

// Opens AURA's real server modules on a throw-away database in a temporary folder.
// Your own data/aura.db is never opened: the run refuses to start unless the database path is inside
// the new temporary folder.
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

export const EVAL_DIR = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
export const ROOT = path.resolve(EVAL_DIR, "..");
const TEXT_MODEL_REL = path.join("models", "Xenova", "all-MiniLM-L6-v2");

/**
 * clock: "fake" (default) makes Date.now() tick 1 ms per call from a fixed start, so runs are exactly
 * repeatable (AURA orders memories by millisecond timestamps, and ties would otherwise depend on timing).
 * Real-model runs use clock: "real" (request pacing and latency need real time).
 */
export async function openIsolated({ clock = "fake" } = {}) {
  if (clock === "fake") {
    let t = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 13, 0, 0, 0);
    Date.now = () => ++t;
  }
  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "aura-eval-"));
  // the local embedding model is copied from the project's model cache (no download)
  const src = path.join(process.env.AURA_EVAL_MODEL_DIR || path.join(ROOT, "data"), TEXT_MODEL_REL);
  if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(src, "onnx"))) {
    throw new Error(`The local embedding model was not found at ${src}. Start AURA once so it downloads its models.`);
  }
  fs.cpSync(src, path.join(dir, TEXT_MODEL_REL), { recursive: true });

  process.env.AURA_DATA_DIR = dir;
  process.env.AURA_NO_WARMUP = "1";
  delete process.env.AURA_DB_PATH;

  // the app logs every extraction; keep the evaluation's own output readable
  if (!process.env.AURA_EVAL_VERBOSE) {
    const log = console.log;
    console.log = (...x) => {
      if (typeof x[0] === "string" && x[0].startsWith("[memory]")) return;
      log(...x);
    };
  }

  const config = await import("../../server/config.mjs");
  const dbm = await import("../../server/db.mjs");
  const inside = (p) => path.resolve(p).startsWith(path.resolve(dir) + path.sep);
  if (path.resolve(config.DATA_DIR) !== path.resolve(dir) || !inside(dbm.DB_PATH)) {
    throw new Error(`Refusing to run: the database (${dbm.DB_PATH}) is not inside the temporary folder ${dir}.`);
  }
  // throw-away database: skip waiting for the disk on every write (results are unaffected)
  dbm.db.exec("PRAGMA synchronous = OFF; PRAGMA journal_mode = MEMORY;");
  const mem = await import("../../server/memory.mjs");
  const models = await import("./cached-models.mjs");
  const gem = await import("./proxy-gemini.mjs");

  return {
    dir,
    config,
    db: dbm.db,
    f32ToBlob: dbm.f32ToBlob,
    saveSettings: dbm.saveSettings,
    mem,
    models,
    gem,
    reset() {
      dbm.db.exec("DELETE FROM memory_proposals; DELETE FROM memories; DELETE FROM messages; DELETE FROM conversations; DELETE FROM settings;");
    },
    cleanup() {
      try {
        dbm.db.close();
      } catch {}
      fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    },
  };
}

// Runs one persona through AURA's real memory pipeline (extraction -> operations -> review) and scores
// the final memory store against the ground truth.
//
// Policies (how memory changes are handled):
//   append  : only "add" is ever applied (no updates, no retirements, no deletions)
//   auto    : every operation is applied immediately          (AURA with "ask before changes" off)
//   gate    : changes to existing memories wait for the user   (AURA default: confirmMemoryChanges on)
//   gateAll : like gate, and new facts are confirmed too       (emulated in the harness: AURA has no such setting)
//
// The extractor is either simulated (known error rates, see makeSimExtractor) or the real Gemini model
// wrapped by the same policy logic. The simulated user approves correct proposals and turns down wrong
// ones, but makes a mistake with probability u.
import { rng, hash, pick } from "./rng.mjs";
import { SLOT, FACT_INDEX, factOf, isTrue, isFiller, newGold, applyEvent, goldFacts, fillerSample } from "./scenarios.mjs";

export const POLICIES = ["append", "auto", "gate", "gateAll"];
const DAY = 86400000;

// "[12] (personal) The user lives in Pune." lines of the extraction prompt
export function parseCandidates(prompt) {
  const out = [];
  const re = /^\[(\d+)\] \((\w+)\) (.*)$/gm;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(prompt))) out.push({ id: Number(m[1]), category: m[2], content: m[3] });
  return out;
}

/**
 * The simulated extractor: returns the operations a correct model would return for the current turn,
 * then injects errors at rate e:
 *   miss            : the correct operation is dropped                     (prob e per fact-bearing turn)
 *   spurious add    : a distractor becomes a false memory                  (prob e per distractor turn)
 *   wrong change    : a TRUE memory shown to the model is retired or overwritten with a false value
 *                                                                          (prob e per non-distractor turn)
 * A correct model can only reference memories it was shown (the candidates in the prompt); when the
 * memory to change is not among them it does what a real model would: it adds the new fact.
 */
export function makeSimExtractor(run) {
  return (args) => {
    if (!/maintain the long-term memory/.test(args.system || "")) throw new Error("unexpected model call in the simulation");
    const { turn, gold, e, r } = run.ctx;
    const ev = turn.event;
    const cands = parseCandidates(args.prompt);
    const idOf = new Map(cands.map((c) => [c.content, c.id]));
    const ops = [];
    const slot = ev.slot ? SLOT[ev.slot] : null;
    const miss = r() < e; // drawn on every turn, in a fixed order, so all policies see the same errors
    const spurious = r() < e;
    const wrong = r() < e;
    const wrongKind = r();
    const victimRoll = r();
    const corruptRoll = r();

    if (ev.type === "add" && !miss) ops.push({ action: "add", content: factOf(ev.slot, ev.value), category: slot.category });
    if (ev.type === "update" && !miss) {
      const id = idOf.get(factOf(ev.slot, ev.from));
      ops.push(id ? { action: "update", memory_id: id, content: factOf(ev.slot, ev.to), category: slot.category } : { action: "add", content: factOf(ev.slot, ev.to), category: slot.category });
    }
    if ((ev.type === "retire" || ev.type === "forget") && !miss) {
      const id = idOf.get(factOf(ev.slot, ev.from));
      if (id) ops.push({ action: ev.type, memory_id: id });
    }
    if (ev.type === "reconfirm" && !idOf.has(factOf(ev.slot, ev.value))) ops.push({ action: "add", content: factOf(ev.slot, ev.value), category: slot.category });
    if (ev.type === "distractor" && spurious) ops.push({ action: "add", content: ev.falseFact, category: "other" });

    if (ev.type !== "distractor" && wrong) {
      const victims = cands.filter((c) => isTrue(c.content, gold) && FACT_INDEX.get(c.content)?.slot !== ev.slot);
      if (victims.length) {
        const v = victims[Math.floor(victimRoll * victims.length)];
        const info = FACT_INDEX.get(v.content);
        let corrupted = null;
        if (info) {
          const unsaid = SLOT[info.slot].values.filter((x) => !(gold.stated.get(info.slot) || new Set()).has(x));
          if (unsaid.length) corrupted = factOf(info.slot, unsaid[Math.floor(corruptRoll * unsaid.length)]);
        }
        const op = wrongKind < 0.5 && corrupted ? { action: "update", memory_id: v.id, content: corrupted, category: info.slot ? SLOT[info.slot].category : "other" } : { action: "retire", memory_id: v.id };
        ops.push(op);
        run.injected.add(`${op.action}:${v.id}`);
        run.counts.injectedWrongChanges++;
      }
    }
    if (miss && ["add", "update", "retire", "forget"].includes(ev.type)) run.counts.injectedMisses++;
    if (ev.type === "distractor" && spurious) run.counts.injectedSpurious++;
    return { operations: ops };
  };
}

/** Wraps an extractor with the policy-specific handling of its output. */
export function withPolicy(run, extractor) {
  return async (args, realGenerateJSON) => {
    const out = await extractor(args, realGenerateJSON);
    let ops = Array.isArray(out?.operations) ? out.operations : [];
    run.counts.opsReturned += ops.length;
    if (run.policy === "append") ops = ops.filter((o) => o.action === "add");
    if (run.policy === "gateAll") {
      const kept = [];
      for (const o of ops) {
        if (o.action !== "add") {
          kept.push(o);
          continue;
        }
        run.counts.prompts++;
        run.counts.addPrompts++;
        const correct = run.judge.addIsCorrect(o.content, run.ctx.gold);
        if (userAccepts(run, correct)) kept.push(o);
        tally(run, correct, userAcceptsLast(run));
        run.decisions.push({ action: "add", content: o.content, judgedCorrect: correct, accepted: userAcceptsLast(run) });
      }
      ops = kept;
    }
    return { ...out, operations: ops };
  };
}

function userAccepts(run, correct) {
  const slip = run.userR() < run.u;
  run._last = correct ? !slip : slip;
  return run._last;
}
const userAcceptsLast = (run) => run._last;

function tally(run, correct, accepted) {
  if (correct && accepted) run.counts.correctAccepted++;
  else if (correct && !accepted) run.counts.correctRejected++;
  else if (!correct && accepted) run.counts.wrongAccepted++;
  else run.counts.wrongRejected++;
}

// Ground-truth judgements for the simulation (exact sentences are known).
export const exactJudge = {
  addIsCorrect: (content, gold) => isTrue(content, gold),
  proposalIsCorrect(p, gold) {
    const target = p.current?.content || "";
    const ti = FACT_INDEX.get(target);
    if (p.action === "update") {
      const ni = FACT_INDEX.get(p.content || "");
      return isTrue(p.content, gold) && !isTrue(target, gold) && !!ti && !!ni && ti.slot === ni.slot;
    }
    if (p.action === "retire") return !isTrue(target, gold);
    if (p.action === "forget") return !!ti && gold.forgotten.some((f) => f.slot === ti.slot && f.value === ti.value);
    return false;
  },
};

function newCounts() {
  return {
    userTurns: 0, extractions: 0, opsReturned: 0, prompts: 0, addPrompts: 0, changePrompts: 0,
    correctAccepted: 0, correctRejected: 0, wrongAccepted: 0, wrongRejected: 0,
    injectedWrongChanges: 0, injectedMisses: 0, injectedSpurious: 0, wrongChangesApplied: 0,
    candidateMissesOnChange: 0, changeTurns: 0, extractionErrors: 0,
  };
}

async function insertFiller(env, content, t) {
  const emb = await env.models.embedText(content);
  env.db
    .prepare("INSERT INTO memories(content, category, status, source, embedding, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, 'other', 'active', 'manual', ?, ?, ?)")
    .run(content, env.f32ToBlob(emb), t, t);
}

/**
 * Runs one persona under one policy. Returns per-persona metrics.
 * opts: { policy, e, u, fillerInitial, fillerPerGap, extractor: "sim" | "real", judge }
 */
export async function runPersona(env, persona, opts) {
  const { policy, e = 0, u = 0, fillerInitial = 30, fillerPerGap = 10 } = opts;
  env.reset();
  env.saveSettings({ autoMemory: true, confirmMemoryChanges: policy === "gate" || policy === "gateAll" });

  const run = {
    policy, e, u, persona,
    ctx: null,
    counts: newCounts(),
    injected: new Set(),
    judge: opts.judge || exactJudge,
    userR: rng(hash(`user|${persona.id}|${policy}|${e}|${u}`)),
    decisions: [], // every review card: what was proposed and what the simulated user decided
  };
  // opts.extractorFn(args, realGenerateJSON, run) lets a runner wrap the real model (e.g. to pace requests)
  const base = opts.extractorFn
    ? (args, realGen) => opts.extractorFn(args, realGen, run)
    : opts.extractor === "real"
      ? (args, realGen) => realGen(args)
      : makeSimExtractor(run);
  env.gem.setHandler(withPolicy(run, base));

  // instrumentation: which applied/accepted operations were injected wrong changes
  const onApplied = (a) => {
    for (const x of a.applied || []) {
      const id = x.op === "update" ? x.replaced : x.id;
      if ((x.op === "update" || x.op === "retire" || x.op === "forget") && run.injected.has(`${x.op}:${id}`)) run.counts.wrongChangesApplied++;
    }
  };
  const onDecision = (d) => {
    if (d.decision === "accepted" && run.injected.has(`${d.action}:${d.memoryId}`)) run.counts.wrongChangesApplied++;
  };
  env.mem.memoryEvents.on("applied", onApplied);
  env.mem.memoryEvents.on("decision", onDecision);

  try {
    const fillers = fillerSample(fillerInitial + fillerPerGap * (persona.sessions.length - 1), `${persona.id}`);
    let fi = 0;
    const t0 = Date.now() - 90 * DAY;
    for (; fi < fillerInitial; fi++) await insertFiller(env, fillers[fi], t0 + fi * 60000);

    const gold = newGold();
    for (let s = 0; s < persona.sessions.length; s++) {
      // other conversations happened between sessions: more (recent) memories
      if (s > 0) for (let k = 0; k < fillerPerGap; k++, fi++) await insertFiller(env, fillers[fi], Date.now());
      const t = Date.now();
      const convId = Number(env.db.prepare("INSERT INTO conversations(started_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?)").run(t, t).lastInsertRowid);
      const msg = env.db.prepare("INSERT INTO messages(conversation_id, role, modality, text, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, 'text', ?, ?)");

      for (let i = 0; i < persona.sessions[s].length; i++) {
        const turn = persona.sessions[s][i];
        applyEvent(gold, turn.event);
        if (turn.assistantFirst) msg.run(convId, "assistant", turn.assistantFirst, Date.now());
        msg.run(convId, "user", turn.user, Date.now());
        msg.run(convId, "assistant", turn.assistant, Date.now());
        run.counts.userTurns++;
        run.ctx = { turn, gold, e, r: rng(hash(`turn|${persona.id}|${s}|${i}|${e}`)) };

        // reachability: was the memory this turn changes among the memories shown to the model?
        if (["update", "retire", "forget"].includes(turn.event.type)) run.counts.changeTurns++;
        const onExtraction = (x) => {
          if (!["update", "retire", "forget"].includes(turn.event.type)) return;
          const target = factOf(turn.event.slot, turn.event.from);
          const row = env.db.prepare("SELECT id FROM memories WHERE content = ? AND status = 'active'").get(target);
          if (row && !x.candidateIds.includes(row.id)) run.counts.candidateMissesOnChange++;
        };
        env.mem.memoryEvents.once("extraction", onExtraction);
        try {
          await env.mem.extractFromConversation(convId);
        } catch (err) {
          // like the app: a failed extraction is retried with the next message (extracted_upto did not move)
          run.counts.extractionErrors++;
          run.lastError = String(err?.message || err);
          if (run.counts.extractionErrors <= 2) console.log(`  extraction error: ${run.lastError}`);
          if (opts.stopOnError) throw err;
        }
        env.mem.memoryEvents.off("extraction", onExtraction);
        run.counts.extractions++;
      }

      // end of session: the user goes through the cards waiting for an OK
      if (policy === "gate" || policy === "gateAll") {
        for (const p of env.mem.listProposals()) {
          run.counts.prompts++;
          run.counts.changePrompts++;
          const correct = run.judge.proposalIsCorrect(p, gold);
          const accepted = userAccepts(run, correct);
          if (accepted) await env.mem.acceptProposal(p.id);
          else env.mem.rejectProposal(p.id);
          tally(run, correct, accepted);
          run.decisions.push({ session: s + 1, action: p.action, current: p.current?.content || null, content: p.content || null, judgedCorrect: correct, accepted });
        }
      }
    }
    if (opts.onFinish) opts.onFinish(env, gold, run);
    return { ...(opts.scorer || score)(env, gold, run), ...run.counts };
  } finally {
    env.mem.memoryEvents.off("applied", onApplied);
    env.mem.memoryEvents.off("decision", onDecision);
    env.gem.setHandler(null);
  }
}

/** Compares the final memory store with the ground truth. */
export function score(env, gold, run) {
  const rows = env.db.prepare("SELECT id, content, status FROM memories").all();
  const active = rows.filter((r) => r.status === "active" && !isFiller(r.content));
  const activeSet = new Set(active.map((r) => r.content));
  const G = goldFacts(gold);
  const correct = G.filter((f) => activeSet.has(f)).length;
  let stale = 0;
  let falseMem = 0;
  for (const r of active) {
    if (isTrue(r.content, gold)) continue;
    const info = FACT_INDEX.get(r.content);
    const wasSaid = info && !info.distractor && (gold.stated.get(info.slot) || new Set()).has(info.value);
    if (wasSaid) stale++;
    else falseMem++;
  }
  const missing = G.filter((f) => !activeSet.has(f));
  const destroyed = missing.filter((f) => rows.some((r) => r.content === f && r.status !== "active")).length;
  const fillerRows = rows.filter((r) => isFiller(r.content));
  const fillerLost = fillerRows.filter((r) => r.status !== "active").length;
  // forgetting: is the forgotten value still stored anywhere?
  let forgetMemResidual = 0;
  let forgetTextResidual = 0;
  for (const f of gold.forgotten) {
    const fact = factOf(f.slot, f.value);
    if (rows.some((r) => r.content === fact)) forgetMemResidual++;
    const n = env.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM messages WHERE text LIKE ?").get(`%${f.value}%`).n;
    if (n > 0) forgetTextResidual++;
  }
  const nActive = active.length;
  const precision = nActive ? correct / nActive : 1;
  const recall = G.length ? correct / G.length : 1;
  return {
    goldFacts: G.length,
    activeFacts: nActive,
    correct,
    stale,
    falseMem,
    missing: missing.length,
    destroyed,
    fillerLost,
    forgets: gold.forgotten.length,
    forgetMemResidual,
    forgetTextResidual,
    precision,
    recall,
    f1: precision + recall ? (2 * precision * recall) / (precision + recall) : 0,
    exactState: correct === G.length && nActive === correct && fillerLost === 0 ? 1 : 0,
  };
}

export { pick };

// Module-resolution hooks for the evaluation harness (registered by register.mjs).
//  - "sharp" (an image library transformers.js loads at start) is replaced by a stub: the evaluation only
//    embeds text, and on Linux the Windows-installed binary of sharp cannot load.
//  - server/gemini.mjs is routed through proxy-gemini.mjs, so a run can either call the real model or a
//    simulated extractor with known error rates.
//  - server/models.mjs is routed through cached-models.mjs, which memoises text embeddings (same model,
//    same vectors; repeated sentences are only embedded once).
const here = (f) => new URL(f, import.meta.url).href;

export async function resolve(specifier, context, next) {
  if (specifier === "sharp") return { url: here("./sharp-stub.mjs"), shortCircuit: true };
  const r = await next(specifier, context);
  const parent = context.parentURL || "";
  if (r.url.endsWith("/server/gemini.mjs") && !parent.endsWith("/eval/lib/proxy-gemini.mjs")) {
    return { ...r, url: here("./proxy-gemini.mjs") };
  }
  if (r.url.endsWith("/server/models.mjs") && !parent.endsWith("/eval/lib/cached-models.mjs")) {
    return { ...r, url: here("./cached-models.mjs") };
  }
  return r;
}

// A tiny made-up dataset in the LongMemEval file format, used only to test the runner without Gemini
// (`npm run eval:lme -- --check-with-sim`). It is NOT LongMemEval data and no result from it is reported.
//
// Format of one LongMemEval instance (as published with the benchmark):
//   question_id, question_type, question, answer, question_date,
//   haystack_session_ids[], haystack_dates[], haystack_sessions[][] of { role, content, has_answer? },
//   answer_session_ids[]
import { rng, hash, pick } from "./rng.mjs";

const CITIES = ["Pune", "Hyderabad", "Chennai", "Jaipur", "Kochi", "Indore"];
const FIRMS = ["Infosys", "Wipro", "Zoho", "Freshworks", "Flipkart", "Swiggy"];
const GAMES = ["chess", "carrom", "badminton", "cricket", "hockey"];

const turn = (role, content, has_answer) => (has_answer ? { role, content, has_answer: true } : { role, content });

export function makeFixture(n = 6, seed = 1) {
  const out = [];
  for (let q = 0; q < n; q++) {
    const r = rng(hash(`fixture|${seed}|${q}`));
    const kind = q % 2 === 0 ? "city" : "employer";
    const a = pick(kind === "city" ? CITIES : FIRMS, r);
    let b = pick(kind === "city" ? CITIES : FIRMS, r);
    if (b === a) b = (kind === "city" ? CITIES : FIRMS).find((x) => x !== a);
    const first = kind === "city" ? `I live in ${a}.` : `I work at ${a}.`;
    const second = kind === "city" ? `I have just moved to ${b}.` : `I now work at ${b}.`;
    const sessions = [];
    const ids = [];
    const dates = [];
    const add = (id, date, turns) => {
      ids.push(id);
      dates.push(date);
      sessions.push(turns);
    };
    add(`q${q}-s1`, "2023/03/02 (Thu) 09:10", [turn("user", first, true), turn("assistant", "Thanks, noted.")]);
    add(`q${q}-d1`, "2023/03/09 (Thu) 18:30", [turn("user", `I like ${pick(GAMES, r)}.`), turn("assistant", "Nice choice.")]);
    add(`q${q}-s2`, "2023/05/20 (Sat) 02:21", [turn("user", second, true), turn("assistant", "Good luck with the change.")]);
    add(`q${q}-d2`, "2023/05/27 (Sat) 11:00", [turn("user", `I like ${pick(GAMES, r)}.`), turn("assistant", "Sounds fun.")]);
    add(`q${q}-d3`, "2023/06/03 (Sat) 20:45", [turn("user", "What is the capital of France?"), turn("assistant", "Paris.")]);
    out.push({
      question_id: `fx${q}`,
      question_type: "knowledge-update",
      question: kind === "city" ? "Where do I live now?" : "Where do I work now?",
      answer: b,
      question_date: "2023/07/01 (Sat) 10:00",
      haystack_session_ids: ids,
      haystack_dates: dates,
      haystack_sessions: sessions,
      answer_session_ids: [`q${q}-s1`, `q${q}-s2`],
    });
  }
  return out;
}

FILE: eval/lib/loose.mjs

// Scoring for memories written by a real model, whose wording differs from the scenario sentences.
// A memory is matched to facts by the VALUES it mentions ("Pune", "Swift", "6 am", "oat milk"), using the
// persona's slots. Example: "The user relocated to Hyderabad from Pune." mentions the current city -> true.
import { SLOT, SLOTS, DISTRACTORS, isFiller } from "./scenarios.mjs";

// other ways a model may write a value
const ALIASES = {
  coffee: { black: ["black coffee", "black"], "with oat milk": ["oat milk"], "with extra sugar": ["extra sugar"], "as a cappuccino": ["cappuccino"] },
  gym: { "6 am": ["6 am", "6am", "6:00 am", "6 a.m."], "7 am": ["7 am", "7am", "7:00 am", "7 a.m."], "6 pm": ["6 pm", "6pm", "6:00 pm", "6 p.m.", "18:00"], "8 pm": ["8 pm", "8pm", "8:00 pm", "8 p.m.", "20:00"] },
  birthday: {
    "12 March": ["12 march", "march 12", "12th march", "march 12th", "12th of march"],
    "3 July": ["3 july", "july 3", "3rd july", "july 3rd", "3rd of july"],
    "21 September": ["21 september", "september 21", "21st september", "september 21st", "21st of september"],
    "8 December": ["8 december", "december 8", "8th december", "december 8th", "8th of december"],
  },
};
const esc = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
const pattern = (alts) => new RegExp(`(^|[^\\p{L}\\p{N}])(${alts.map(esc).join("|")})(?=$|[^\\p{L}\\p{N}])`, "iu");

const MATCHERS = [];
for (const s of SLOTS) for (const v of s.values) MATCHERS.push({ slot: s.key, value: v, re: pattern(ALIASES[s.key]?.[v] || [v]) });
for (const d of DISTRACTORS) MATCHERS.push({ slot: d.slot, value: d.value, distractor: true, re: pattern([d.value]) });

/** Every (slot, value) a memory sentence mentions. */
export function mentions(content) {
  return MATCHERS.filter((m) => m.re.test(content));
}

const trueNow = (m, gold) => !m.distractor && m.slot && gold.state.get(m.slot) === m.value;
const saidBefore = (m, gold) => !m.distractor && m.slot && (gold.stated.get(m.slot) || new Set()).has(m.value);

// Wording a real model uses (found in the first Gemini run, 13 Oct 2026):
//  - facts about people in the user's life ("The user's friend Rohan bought a Thar.") are legitimate memories;
//  - hypotheticals kept as hypotheticals ("If the user had a cat, they would name her Luna.") are noise,
//    not a false belief about the user;
//  - a fact that ended can be recorded as such ("The user finished leading project Lotus and is between
//    projects."), which is correct when the user retired that fact (not when they asked to forget it).
const THIRD_PARTY = /\b(friend|cousin|brother|colleague|neighbou?r|uncle|aunt|mother|father|mom|dad|wife|husband|partner)\b/i;
const HYPOTHETICAL = /\b(if|would|hypothetical(ly)?)\b/i;
const ENDED = /\b(no longer|anymore|finished|wrapped up|between projects|stopped|quit|sold|gave up|given up|passed away|died|unemployed|not working|formerly|used to|previously)\b/i;

/**
 * true | ended (correct record that a fact stopped being true) | stale | false |
 * third-party (about someone else; allowed) | hypothetical (noise) | other (mentions no known value)
 */
export function classify(content, gold) {
  const ms = mentions(content);
  if (!ms.length) return "other";
  const own = ms.filter((m) => !m.distractor);
  if (!own.length) {
    if (THIRD_PARTY.test(content)) return "third-party";
    if (HYPOTHETICAL.test(content)) return "hypothetical";
    return "false";
  }
  if (own.some((m) => trueNow(m, gold))) return "true";
  const retired = (m) => gold.state.get(m.slot) == null && !gold.forgotten.some((f) => f.slot === m.slot && f.value === m.value);
  if (ENDED.test(content) && own.some((m) => saidBefore(m, gold) && retired(m))) return "ended";
  if (own.some((m) => saidBefore(m, gold))) return "stale";
  return "false";
}

const GOOD = new Set(["true", "ended"]);

export const looseJudge = {
  addIsCorrect: (content, gold) => GOOD.has(classify(content, gold)) || classify(content, gold) === "third-party",
  proposalIsCorrect(p, gold) {
    const target = p.current?.content || "";
    if (p.action === "update") {
      if (GOOD.has(classify(target, gold))) return false; // never replace a fact that is still true
      const oldSlots = new Set(mentions(target).map((m) => m.slot));
      const newM = mentions(p.content || "").filter((m) => trueNow(m, gold));
      // the new value of the same fact, or a note that the fact ended
      return newM.some((n) => oldSlots.has(n.slot)) || (classify(p.content || "", gold) === "ended" && mentions(p.content || "").some((m) => oldSlots.has(m.slot)));
    }
    if (p.action === "retire") return classify(target, gold) !== "true" && !isFiller(target);
    if (p.action === "forget") return mentions(target).some((m) => gold.forgotten.some((f) => f.slot === m.slot && f.value === m.value));
    return false;
  },
};

/** Final-state score for model-written memories (the counterpart of harness.score). */
export function looseScore(env, gold) {
  const rows = env.db.prepare("SELECT id, content, status FROM memories").all();
  const active = rows.filter((r) => r.status === "active" && !isFiller(r.content));
  const goldPairs = [...gold.state].filter(([, v]) => v != null);
  const correct = goldPairs.filter(([k, v]) => active.some((r) => mentions(r.content).some((m) => m.slot === k && m.value === v))).length;
  const cls = active.map((r) => classify(r.content, gold));
  const n = (c) => cls.filter((x) => x === c).length;
  // third-party facts are allowed and not counted; hypotheticals count as errors (they are not facts about the user)
  const scored = n("true") + n("ended") + n("stale") + n("false") + n("hypothetical");
  const precision = scored ? (n("true") + n("ended")) / scored : 1;
  const recall = goldPairs.length ? correct / goldPairs.length : 1;
  const fillerLost = rows.filter((r) => isFiller(r.content) && r.status !== "active").length;
  let forgetMemResidual = 0;
  for (const f of gold.forgotten) if (rows.some((r) => mentions(r.content).some((m) => m.slot === f.slot && m.value === f.value))) forgetMemResidual++;
  return {
    goldFacts: goldPairs.length,
    activeFacts: active.length,
    correct,
    trueMem: n("true"),
    endedMem: n("ended"),
    stale: n("stale"),
    falseMem: n("false"),
    hypotheticalMem: n("hypothetical"),
    thirdPartyMem: n("third-party"),
    otherMem: n("other"),
    fillerLost,
    forgets: gold.forgotten.length,
    forgetMemResidual,
    precision,
    recall,
    f1: precision + recall ? (2 * precision * recall) / (precision + recall) : 0,
  };
}

export { SLOT };

// Stands in for server/gemini.mjs during evaluation.
// Without a handler every call goes to the real Gemini code. With a handler (simulation runs, or a
// policy wrapper around the real model) the handler decides what the memory extractor "returns".
import * as real from "../../server/gemini.mjs";

export const usage = real.usage; // token/latency totals of real calls
export const createLiveToken = real.createLiveToken;
export const transcribeSegments = real.transcribeSegments;

export const sim = { calls: 0 };
let handler = null;

/** handler(args, realGenerateJSON) -> parsed JSON. Pass null to go back to the real model. */
export function setHandler(fn) {
  handler = fn;
}

export const hasKey = () => (handler ? true : real.hasKey());

export async function generateJSON(args) {
  if (!handler) return real.generateJSON(args);
  sim.calls++;
  return handler(args, real.generateJSON);
}

FILE: eval/lib/rng.mjs

// Small deterministic helpers so every run can be reproduced from its seed.

/** 32-bit FNV-1a hash of a string. */
export function hash(str) {
  let h = 0x811c9dc5;
  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    h ^= str.charCodeAt(i);
    h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);
  }
  return h >>> 0;
}

/** mulberry32 PRNG: returns a function giving floats in [0, 1). */
export function rng(seed) {
  let a = seed >>> 0;
  return () => {
    a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
    let t = a;
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

export const pick = (arr, r) => arr[Math.floor(r() * arr.length)];

export function shuffle(arr, r) {
  const a = arr.slice();
  for (let i = a.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(r() * (i + 1));
    [a[i], a[j]] = [a[j], a[i]];
  }
  return a;
}

// Synthetic multi-session dialogues with known ground truth.
//
// A persona has 8 of the 12 "slots" below (city, employer, ...). Over 5 sessions the user states facts,
// later changes some (update), says some are no longer true (retire), asks AURA to forget some, repeats
// some (reconfirm), and says things that must NOT become memories (distractors: hypotheticals, questions,
// assistant suggestions, facts about other people). Every user turn carries the event that produced it,
// so the true memory state is known after every turn.
//
// All sentences are written by the authors of this evaluation (no real user data).
import { rng, hash, pick, shuffle } from "./rng.mjs";

const fill = (tpl, v) => tpl.replaceAll("{v}", v);

    queries: ["When is my birthday?", "What date is my birthday?"],

export const SLOT = Object.fromEntries(SLOTS.map((s) => [s.key, s]));
export const factOf = (slotKey, v) => fill(SLOT[slotKey].fact, v);

// Statements that must not become memories. falseFact/falseValue describe the wrong memory an extractor
// could create from them (used to inject errors in simulation and to score real runs).
export const DISTRACTORS = [
  { kind: "hypothetical", user: "If I ever moved to Goa, I'd spend every evening on the beach.", slot: "city", value: "Goa", falseFact: "The user lives in Goa." },
  { kind: "question", user: "What's the weather like in Shimla today?", slot: "city", value: "Shimla", falseFact: "The user lives in Shimla." },
  { kind: "assistant-suggestion", assistantFirst: "Since you enjoy languages, you could try Italian next.", user: "Hmm, maybe, I'll think about it.", slot: "language", value: "Italian", falseFact: "The user is learning Italian." },
  { kind: "third-party", user: "My friend Rohan just bought a Thar, it looks great.", slot: "car", value: "Thar", falseFact: "The user drives a Thar." },
  { kind: "third-party", user: "My cousin works at Google in Zurich.", slot: "employer", value: "Google", falseFact: "The user works at Google." },
  { kind: "hypothetical", user: "If I had a cat I would call her Luna.", slot: "pet", value: "Luna", falseFact: "The user has a cat named Luna." },
  { kind: "one-off", user: "Can you set a timer for ten minutes?", slot: null, value: "timer", falseFact: "The user set a timer for ten minutes." },
  { kind: "general-knowledge", user: "Is it true that octopuses have three hearts?", slot: "hobby", value: "marine biology", falseFact: "The user's main hobby is marine biology." },
];

const REPLIES = ["Got it.", "Okay, noted.", "Thanks for telling me.", "Understood.", "Sure."];

// Unrelated true facts that fill the memory store, as months of earlier use would.
// Several are deliberately close to the persona facts (friends' cities, cuisines), as real stores are.
function buildFillerPool() {
  const names = ["Rohan", "Aditya", "Vikram", "Neha", "Pooja", "Arjun", "Ishaan", "Tanvi", "Kabir", "Riya", "Siddharth", "Aisha"];
  const cities = ["Mumbai", "Delhi", "Surat", "Nagpur", "Mysuru", "Kochi", "Patna", "Ranchi", "Guwahati", "Dehradun"];
  const out = [];
  for (const t of ["Chennai Super Kings", "Mumbai Indians", "Royal Challengers Bengaluru", "Kolkata Knight Riders", "Rajasthan Royals", "Delhi Capitals", "Punjab Kings", "Gujarat Titans"])
    out.push(`The user's favourite cricket team is ${t}.`);
  for (const n of names) for (const c of cities) out.push(`The user's friend ${n} lives in ${c}.`);
  for (const p of ["Japan", "Iceland", "Ladakh", "Bali", "Norway", "Peru", "Kenya", "Vietnam", "Scotland", "New Zealand"])
    out.push(`The user wants to visit ${p} someday.`);
  for (const m of ["Interstellar", "3 Idiots", "Lagaan", "Dune", "Inception", "Swades", "Oppenheimer", "Dangal", "Arrival", "Piku"])
    out.push(`The user recently watched ${m}.`);
  for (const n of names) for (const t of ["payments", "search", "mobile", "data", "security", "design", "QA", "infra"])
    out.push(`The user's colleague ${n} handles the ${t} team.`);
  for (const d of ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]) out.push(`The user has a haircut booked for ${d}.`);
  for (const b of ["Sapiens", "Atomic Habits", "The Alchemist", "Wings of Fire", "Ikigai", "Deep Work", "The Guide", "Malgudi Days", "Educated"])
    out.push(`The user is reading ${b}.`);
  for (const l of ["ThinkPad", "MacBook Air", "Dell XPS", "HP Spectre", "Asus Zenbook", "Acer Swift"]) out.push(`The user's laptop is a ${l}.`);
  for (const s of ["window", "aisle"]) out.push(`The user prefers ${s} seats on flights.`);
  for (const c of ["Bengali", "Punjabi", "Kerala", "Chettinad", "Gujarati", "Thai", "Mexican", "Lebanese"]) out.push(`The user's favourite cuisine is ${c}.`);
  for (const f of ["Barcelona", "Arsenal", "Liverpool", "Bayern Munich", "Real Madrid", "Juventus"]) out.push(`The user supports ${f} in football.`);
  for (const a of ["A. R. Rahman", "Arijit Singh", "Shreya Ghoshal", "Coldplay", "Prateek Kuhad", "Kishore Kumar"]) out.push(`The user's favourite singer is ${a}.`);
  for (const n of names) for (const a of ["parrot", "rabbit", "tortoise", "labrador"]) out.push(`The user's neighbour ${n} has a ${a}.`);
  for (const i of ["a standing desk", "new headphones", "a smartwatch", "a bicycle", "an air purifier", "a coffee grinder", "running shoes"])
    out.push(`The user bought ${i} last month.`);
  for (const r of ["uncle", "aunt", "grandmother", "cousin"]) for (const c of cities) out.push(`The user's ${r} lives in ${c}.`);
  return out;
}
export const FILLER_POOL = buildFillerPool();
const FILLER_SET = new Set(FILLER_POOL);

/** A deterministic sample of n filler facts. */
export function fillerSample(n, seedStr) {
  if (n > FILLER_POOL.length) throw new Error(`filler pool has only ${FILLER_POOL.length} facts`);
  return shuffle(FILLER_POOL, rng(hash(`filler|${seedStr}`))).slice(0, n);
}

// content -> { slot, value, distractor? } for every sentence the simulation can write
export const FACT_INDEX = new Map();
for (const s of SLOTS) for (const v of s.values) FACT_INDEX.set(factOf(s.key, v), { slot: s.key, value: v });
for (const d of DISTRACTORS) FACT_INDEX.set(d.falseFact, { slot: d.slot, value: d.value, distractor: true });

export const isFiller = (content) => FILLER_SET.has(content);

// ---- ground truth --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

export function newGold() {
  return { state: new Map(), stated: new Map(), forgotten: [] };
}

export function applyEvent(gold, ev) {
  const said = (k, v) => {
    if (!gold.stated.has(k)) gold.stated.set(k, new Set());
    gold.stated.get(k).add(v);
  };
  if (ev.type === "add") {
    gold.state.set(ev.slot, ev.value);
    said(ev.slot, ev.value);
  } else if (ev.type === "update") {
    gold.state.set(ev.slot, ev.to);
    said(ev.slot, ev.to);
  } else if (ev.type === "retire") {
    gold.state.set(ev.slot, null);
  } else if (ev.type === "forget") {
    gold.forgotten.push({ slot: ev.slot, value: ev.from });
    gold.state.set(ev.slot, null);
  }
}

/** Is this exact memory sentence true right now? (fillers are always true) */
export function isTrue(content, gold) {
  if (isFiller(content)) return true;
  const info = FACT_INDEX.get(content);
  if (!info || info.distractor) return false;
  return gold.state.get(info.slot) === info.value;
}

/** The facts that should be active right now (persona facts only). */
export function goldFacts(gold) {
  const out = [];
  for (const [k, v] of gold.state) if (v != null) out.push(factOf(k, v));
  return out;
}

// ---- personas ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * sessions: [[turn, ...], ...]; turn = { event, user, assistantFirst, assistant }.
 * event types: add | update | retire | forget | reconfirm | distractor
 */
export function makePersona(seed, idx, { nSlots = 8, nSessions = 5 } = {}) {
  const r = rng(hash(`persona|${seed}|${idx}`));
  const slots = shuffle(SLOTS, r).slice(0, nSlots);
  const gold = newGold();
  const distractors = shuffle(DISTRACTORS, r);
  let dIdx = 0;

  const fresh = (slot) => {
    const used = gold.stated.get(slot.key) || new Set();
    const opts = slot.values.filter((v) => !used.has(v));
    return opts.length ? pick(opts, r) : null;
  };
  const reply = () => pick(REPLIES, r);
  const mk = (event, user, assistantFirst = null) => {
    applyEvent(gold, event);
    return { event, user, assistantFirst, assistant: reply() };
  };
  const add = (slot) => {
    const v = fresh(slot);
    return mk({ type: "add", slot: slot.key, value: v }, fill(slot.add, v));
  };
  const reconfirm = (slot) => {
    const v = gold.state.get(slot.key);
    const s = fill(slot.add, v);
    return mk({ type: "reconfirm", slot: slot.key, value: v }, `Like I said, ${s[0].toLowerCase()}${s.slice(1)}`);
  };
  const distractor = () => {
    const d = distractors[dIdx++ % distractors.length];
    return mk({ type: "distractor", kind: d.kind, slot: d.slot, value: d.value, falseFact: d.falseFact }, d.user, d.assistantFirst || null);
  };
  const change = (slot) => {
    const cur = gold.state.get(slot.key);
    if (cur == null) {
      const v = fresh(slot);
      return v ? add(slot) : null; // re-introduce a slot that was retired or forgotten
    }
    const roll = r();
    const nv = fresh(slot);
    if (roll < 0.55 && slot.update && nv) return mk({ type: "update", slot: slot.key, from: cur, to: nv }, fill(slot.update, nv));
    if (roll < 0.8 && slot.retire) return mk({ type: "retire", slot: slot.key, from: cur }, slot.retire);
    if (roll < 0.9 || (!slot.update && !slot.retire)) return mk({ type: "forget", slot: slot.key, from: cur }, `Please forget what I told you about ${slot.label}.`);
    if (slot.update && nv) return mk({ type: "update", slot: slot.key, from: cur, to: nv }, fill(slot.update, nv));
    return mk({ type: "retire", slot: slot.key, from: cur }, slot.retire);
  };

  // Turns are generated in the order they are spoken, so the ground truth is replayed correctly.
  const sessions = [];
  // session 1: four facts
  sessions.push(slots.slice(0, 4).map(add));
  // session 2: the other four, one repeated fact and one distractor, in random order
  {
    const plan = shuffle(["a4", "a5", "a6", "a7", "re", "d"], r);
    sessions.push(
      plan.map((p) =>
        p === "re" ? reconfirm(pick(slots.slice(0, 4).filter((s) => gold.state.get(s.key) != null), r)) : p === "d" ? distractor() : add(slots[Number(p[1])])
      )
    );
  }
  // later sessions: two changes, one distractor, sometimes a repeated fact
  for (let s = 2; s < nSessions; s++) {
    const plan = shuffle(["c", "c", "d", ...(r() < 0.5 ? ["re"] : [])], r);
    const touched = new Set();
    const turns = [];
    for (const p of plan) {
      if (p === "d") turns.push(distractor());
      else if (p === "re") {
        const opts = slots.filter((x) => gold.state.get(x.key) != null && !touched.has(x.key));
        if (opts.length) turns.push(reconfirm(pick(opts, r)));
      } else {
        const opts = slots.filter((x) => !touched.has(x.key));
        for (const slot of shuffle(opts, r)) {
          const t = change(slot);
          if (t) {
            touched.add(slot.key);
            turns.push(t);
            break;
          }
        }
      }
    }
    sessions.push(turns);
  }
  return { id: `${seed}-${idx}`, seed, idx, slots: slots.map((s) => s.key), sessions, finalGold: gold };
}

// Summary statistics and file output.
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

export const mean = (xs) => (xs.length ? xs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / xs.length : NaN);

export function sd(xs) {
  if (xs.length < 2) return 0;
  const m = mean(xs);
  return Math.sqrt(xs.reduce((a, x) => a + (x - m) ** 2, 0) / (xs.length - 1));
}

/** Half-width of a normal-approximation 95% confidence interval of the mean. */
export const ci95 = (xs) => (xs.length > 1 ? (1.96 * sd(xs)) / Math.sqrt(xs.length) : 0);

/** Wilson 95% interval for a proportion k/n, returned as [lo, hi]. */
export function wilson(k, n) {
  if (!n) return [NaN, NaN];
  const z = 1.96;
  const p = k / n;
  const d = 1 + (z * z) / n;
  const c = (p + (z * z) / (2 * n)) / d;
  const h = (z * Math.sqrt((p * (1 - p)) / n + (z * z) / (4 * n * n))) / d;
  return [c - h, c + h];
}

export const fmt = (x, digits = 3) => (Number.isFinite(x) ? x.toFixed(digits) : "n/a");
export const pm = (xs, digits = 3) => `${fmt(mean(xs), digits)} Â± ${fmt(ci95(xs), digits)}`;

export function toCSV(rows) {
  if (!rows.length) return "";
  const cols = Object.keys(rows[0]);
  const esc = (v) => {
    const s = v == null ? "" : typeof v === "number" ? String(Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6) : String(v);
    return /[",\n]/.test(s) ? `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : s;
  };
  return [cols.join(","), ...rows.map((r) => cols.map((c) => esc(r[c])).join(","))].join("\n") + "\n";
}

/** Reads CSV written by toCSV (quoted fields, doubled quotes). Returns objects keyed by the header. */
export function parseCSV(text) {
  const out = [];
  let row = [], cell = "", q = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    const c = text[i];
    if (q) {
      if (c === '"' && text[i + 1] === '"') { cell += '"'; i++; } else if (c === '"') q = false; else cell += c;
    } else if (c === '"') q = true;
    else if (c === ",") { row.push(cell); cell = ""; }
    else if (c === "\n" || c === "\r") { if (c === "\r" && text[i + 1] === "\n") i++; row.push(cell); cell = ""; if (row.some((x) => x !== "")) out.push(row); row = []; }
    else cell += c;
  }
  if (cell || row.length) { row.push(cell); out.push(row); }
  const [head = [], ...body] = out;
  return body.map((r) => Object.fromEntries(head.map((h, i) => [h, r[i] ?? ""])));
}

export function mdTable(header, rows) {
  return [`| ${header.join(" | ")} |`, `|${header.map(() => "---").join("|")}|`, ...rows.map((r) => `| ${r.join(" | ")} |`)].join("\n");
}

/** eval/results/<name>/<timestamp>/ */
export function resultDir(evalDir, name) {
  const t = new Date();
  const p2 = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
  const stamp = `${t.getFullYear()}${p2(t.getMonth() + 1)}${p2(t.getDate())}-${p2(t.getHours())}${p2(t.getMinutes())}${p2(t.getSeconds())}`;
  const dir = path.join(evalDir, "results", name, stamp);
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  return dir;
}

export function writeJSON(file, obj) {
  fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2) + "\n");
}

// ---- resumable runs: rows are appended to a .jsonl checkpoint as each unit of work finishes ----

/** The output folder: the one given with --out (to resume a run), or a new timestamped one. */
export function outDir(evalDir, name, given) {
  if (given) {
    fs.mkdirSync(given, { recursive: true });
    return path.resolve(given);
  }
  return resultDir(evalDir, name);
}

export function appendRows(dir, file, rows) {
  if (rows.length) fs.appendFileSync(path.join(dir, file), rows.map((r) => JSON.stringify(r)).join("\n") + "\n");
}

export function readRows(dir, file) {
  const p = path.join(dir, file);
  if (!fs.existsSync(p)) return [];
  return fs.readFileSync(p, "utf8").split("\n").filter(Boolean).map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
}

/** Stops starting new work after `seconds` (0 = no limit). */
export function budget(seconds) {
  const t0 = performance.now(); // real time, also when Date.now() is the simulated clock
  return () => seconds > 0 && (performance.now() - t0) / 1000 > seconds;
}

# Checking the automatic labels by hand

Open annotation.csv. For each row, read the memory, look up that persona below, and write one label in human_label (without looking at auto_label first if you can). Ideally a second person labels a copy independently.

| label | use when the memory... |
|---|---|
| true | states something that is true about the user at the end |
| ended | correctly says that a fact the user retired is over ("finished the Lotus project") |
| stale | states something the user said earlier that is no longer true, or something the user asked to forget |
| false | states something the user never said about themselves (misread, invented) |
| hypothetical | keeps a hypothetical or a maybe as a memory ("if the user had a cat...") |
| third-party | is a fact about someone else the user mentioned (allowed) |
| other | none of the above (write why in notes) |

## Persona 1-0

Session 1: "My main hobby is chess." "I'm learning German." "I'm eggetarian." "I take my coffee black."
Session 2: "My dog is called Tiger." "I live in Kolkata." "Is it true that octopuses have three hearts?" "Like I said, my main hobby is chess." "I go to the gym at 6 am every day." "My sister's name is Priya."
Session 3: "If I ever moved to Goa, I'd spend every evening on the beach." "Correction, my dog's name is actually Mithu." "These days I take my coffee with extra sugar." "Like I said, my main hobby is chess."
Session 4: "I moved my gym time to 7 am." "If I had a cat I would call her Luna." "Please forget what I told you about my sister."
Session 5: "Like I said, i live in Kolkata." "My new main hobby is cycling." "I stopped going to the gym." "What's the weather like in Shimla today?"

Truth at the end: hobby: cycling; language: German; diet: eggetarian; coffee: with extra sugar; pet: Mithu; city: Kolkata; gym: no longer true; sister: no longer true. Asked to forget: sister (Priya).

## Choosing the minimum score

Trade-off for the hybrid score at k = 6: "found" = questions about a stored fact that get it among the results; "noise" = questions about something the user never stated (or that is no longer true) that still return memories (unrelated ones). 714 such questions per size.

\begin{document}

\title{Ask Before You Remember: An Empirical Study of Approval-Gated\\Long-Term Memory in a Personal LLM Assistant}

\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Author Name}
\IEEEauthorblockA{Department, Institution\\
City, Country\\
email@example.com}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Personal assistants built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly keep a long-term memory that a model-driven
\emph{extractor} edits after every conversation: it adds facts and also rewrites, retires and deletes the ones already stored.
When the extractor is wrong, the assistant silently loses or corrupts something true about its user.
We study one design response in AURA, a local voice-and-text assistant: changes to existing memories are not applied but
\emph{proposed}, and wait for the user's approval, while the replaced fact is kept as history with its source.
We evaluate this gate on AURA's real memory code, database and embedding model in four ways:
(i) simulated extractor errors and user slips over scripted multi-session personas,
(ii) a measurement of whether the extractor is shown the memory it is asked to change,
(iii) a real Gemini extractor with value-based scoring and human annotation, and
(iv) the LongMemEval knowledge-update questions.
Compared with applying every operation automatically, the gate removed \nn\% of destroyed true facts at $e=0.2$ at a cost of \nn{} review
prompts per 100 turns. We also find that \nn\% of change requests cannot be carried out because the target memory is not among the
candidates shown to the extractor, and that a one-line change to candidate selection raises this to \nn\%.
The harness, scenarios and all result files are released.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
LLM agents, long-term memory, human-in-the-loop, memory update, personal assistants, evaluation
\end{IEEEkeywords}

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Introduction}
A personal assistant is only as useful as what it remembers about its user, and what it remembers is increasingly decided
by an LLM. After each conversation an \emph{extractor} reads the new messages and returns operations on a memory store:
\textsf{add} a fact, \textsf{update} one that changed, \textsf{retire} one that stopped being true, or \textsf{forget} one the user asked it to drop.
Systems that only append facts keep outdated values next to new ones and answer inconsistently once a fact changes
\cite{patel2026supersede,chao2026stale,temporalmemeval}. Systems that let the extractor rewrite memory freely trade this for a different
risk: a single mistaken \textsf{update} or \textsf{retire} destroys a true fact, and the user never learns that it happened.

AURA, a local assistant we built on top of the Gemini Live web console \cite{liveconsole}, takes a middle path.
New facts are stored directly, but every change to an existing memory becomes a \emph{proposal} that the user accepts, edits or rejects.
The old fact is never overwritten: it is kept as history and linked to its successor, and every memory records the conversation it came from.
Whether such a gate actually helps---how much damage it prevents, what it costs in prompts, and what it misses---has not, to our knowledge,
been measured; the governance literature proposes write gates and provenance but mostly as architecture \cite{lam2026ssgm,lin2026survey}
(Section~\ref{sec:related}).

We ask four questions.
\textbf{RQ1:} How much does the gate reduce harmful changes compared with auto-applying them, at what review burden, and how does this depend on the extractor's error rate and on the user's own slips?
\textbf{RQ2:} Can the extractor carry out a change at all---is the memory it must change among the candidates it is shown?
\textbf{RQ3:} Do the conclusions hold with a real extractor (Gemini) instead of a simulated one?
\textbf{RQ4:} What does gating cost in answer accuracy on a public benchmark (LongMemEval knowledge-update questions \cite{wu2024longmemeval})?

\noindent\textbf{Contributions.}
(1) A concrete approval-gated memory design with provenance, history and a forget operation, implemented in a working assistant (Section~\ref{sec:design}).
(2) A reproducible harness that runs AURA's \emph{real} memory code on a throw-away database with a simulated or real extractor, scripted personas with known ground truth, and metrics that expose damage that accuracy hides (Section~\ref{sec:method}).
(3) Evidence on the gate's benefit, burden and failure modes, including a candidate-visibility limit of the extractor and a user-slip failure that no longer re-proposes a rejected change (Section~\ref{sec:results}).
(4) A real-model and benchmark evaluation with human-annotated agreement for the scorer (Section~\ref{sec:results}).

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}
\noindent\textbf{Memory benchmarks and systems.}
LongMemEval \cite{wu2024longmemeval} and LoCoMo \cite{maharana2024locomo} evaluate whether assistants recall information across long, multi-session conversations;
LongMemEval includes a knowledge-update category in which a fact changes and the latest value is the right answer.
Mem0 \cite{chhikara2025mem0} is a widely used memory layer that extracts and consolidates memories with an LLM.
These works measure answer quality; they do not ask who approves the edits the extractor makes.

\noindent\textbf{Keeping memory current.}
Supersede \cite{patel2026supersede} shows that agents with a bounded memory fail to replace outdated values and that the failure grows with history length.
STALE \cite{chao2026stale} builds 400 scenarios in which a later observation invalidates an earlier memory without negating it; the best model it evaluates reaches 55.2\% overall.
Reddy and Challaram \cite{reddy2026assembly} resolve conflicts at \emph{query} time with a deterministic step rather than at ingestion.
An independent evaluation of an open-source Mem0 release \cite{temporalmemeval} (a repository, not a peer-reviewed paper) reports that extraction only adds memories, so old and new values coexist, and that ordering memories by time repairs most knowledge-update errors.
All of these treat the update decision as automatic. We study the decision that precedes them: whether an automatic edit should be applied at all.

\noindent\textbf{Governance and provenance.}
SSGM \cite{lam2026ssgm} proposes a governance layer between agent and store with pre-write validation against core facts, provenance-grounded reads and reversible reconciliation; it is presented as an architecture without an empirical evaluation.
A recent survey of long-term memory security \cite{lin2026survey} names provenance failure and write-gate validation as recurring gaps and states that updates must not bypass authorisation.
Neither describes a user-approval step, and neither measures one.

\noindent\textbf{User control.}
MemCtrl \cite{memctrl2026} tests whether memory systems and two production chatbots obey instructions such as ``do not store'' and ``forget''; none follows all of them reliably.
Studies of how people perceive assistant memory and its privacy risks \cite{zhang2024ghost,zhang2025perceptions,ainever2026} and work on helping users revise what an AI memory holds \cite{vaithilingam2025semantic} motivate user-facing control.
We add a measurement of a specific control---approval of changes---on an extractor's output, with the extractor's and the user's errors both varied.

\noindent\textbf{Gap.}
To our knowledge, none of the work above measures how an approval gate trades prevented damage against review burden while extractor errors and user slips vary, or checks that the extractor is shown the memory it is asked to change. This is what we measure; a literature search cannot prove that no such study exists.

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{System Design}\label{sec:design}
\subsection{Overview}
AURA is a local assistant (Node.js server, SQLite, React front end) derived from the Gemini Live web console \cite{liveconsole}. Memories live in one table with a status
(\textit{active}, \textit{superseded}, \textit{outdated}), a category, a text, a sentence embedding, and provenance fields: the \emph{source} (conversation, meeting or manual), the originating conversation or meeting, and the id of the memory that replaced it. Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline} shows the flow.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  box/.style={draw,rounded corners=1pt,align=center,font=\scriptsize,inner sep=2.5pt,minimum height=6.5mm,fill=black!4},
  gate/.style={box,fill=blue!10,draw=blue!60!black},
  >=Stealth]
\node[box] (msg) at (0.8,0) {New\\messages};
\node[box] (ext) at (3.0,0) {Extractor\\(Gemini)};
\node[box] (cand) at (3.0,1.25) {Candidates: 12 searched\\+ 8 most recent};
\node[box] (ops) at (5.6,0) {Operations};
\node[box] (add) at (4.0,-1.35) {add};
\node[gate] (prop) at (7.2,-1.35) {update / retire /\\forget $\rightarrow$ proposal};
\node[gate] (user) at (7.2,-2.55) {User: accept,\\edit or reject};
\node[box] (store) at (4.0,-2.55) {Memory store\\(active + history + source)};
\draw[->] (msg)--(ext);
\draw[->] (cand)--(ext);
\draw[->] (ext)--(ops);
\draw[->] (ops.south)--(add.north);
\draw[->] (ops.south)--(prop.north);
\draw[->] (prop)--(user);
\draw[->] (add)--(store);
\draw[->] (user)--(store);
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Memory pipeline. Only memories shown as candidates can be changed; additions are stored directly, changes to existing memories go through the user (shaded).}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Extraction and Operations}
After a conversation, the extractor receives the new messages, a short window of earlier context, and \emph{candidate memories}: the 12 stored memories most similar to the new user text plus the 8 most recently confirmed. It returns structured JSON operations (\textsf{add}, \textsf{update}, \textsf{retire}, \textsf{forget}), each referring to a candidate by id. AURA only applies a change to a memory that was among the candidates, so a change whose target was not shown cannot be carried out; Section~\ref{sec:results} measures how often this happens.

\subsection{Approval Gate}
With the setting ``ask before changing memories'' on (the default), \textsf{update}, \textsf{retire} and \textsf{forget} on an existing memory are written to a proposal queue instead of the store. The user sees the current memory and the proposed change and can accept it, edit the wording of an update before accepting, or reject it. A rejected proposal is never proposed again for that memory, so that the user is not asked repeatedly. \textsf{add} is applied directly. A \emph{gate-all} variant that also confirms additions is evaluated by emulation (AURA has no such setting).

\subsection{History, Provenance and Forget}
An accepted update keeps the old memory with status \textit{superseded} and a pointer to its successor; a retirement marks it \textit{outdated}. Retrieval uses only active memories, but history and source remain inspectable. \textsf{forget} deletes the memory row; it does not delete the conversation text it was extracted from, which our evaluation measures as a residual.

\subsection{Retrieval}
Search embeds the query with a local MiniLM model \cite{wang2020minilm} and scores each memory $d$ as
$s(q,d)=0.85\cos(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{d})+0.15\,\ell(q,d)$, where $\ell$ is the token overlap $|Q\cap D|/\sqrt{|Q||D|}$; results below a minimum score of $0.25$ are dropped (0.1 when only keyword overlap is available). The same function selects the extractor's candidates.

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Evaluation Method}\label{sec:method}
\subsection{Experiments}
Table~\ref{tab:exps} lists the five experiments. All run AURA's real server modules, SQLite schema and embedding model on a throw-away database inside a temporary folder; the harness refuses to start if the database path lies elsewhere, so the user's own data is never touched.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\footnotesize
\caption{Experiments. ``Sim'' = simulated component, ``real'' = AURA code or Gemini.}
\label{tab:exps}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
 & Question & Extractor & Data \\
\midrule
1 & RQ1: policies vs.\ $e$, $u$ & sim & personas \\
2 & retrieval of stored facts & -- & personas \\
3 & RQ2: candidate visibility & -- & stores of $N$ facts \\
4 & RQ3: real extractor & Gemini & personas \\
5 & RQ4: public benchmark & Gemini & LongMemEval \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Scenarios}
Each synthetic persona has 8 of 12 fact types (city, employer, dog, sister, diet, gym time, language, car, project, coffee, hobby, birthday) over 5 sessions and about 20.5 user turns. Facts are stated, later updated (``I've just moved to Hyderabad''), retired (``I stopped going to the gym''), forgotten on request (``Please forget what I told you about my car''), repeated, and mixed with four kinds of distractors that must not become memories: hypotheticals, questions, an assistant's suggestion, and facts about friends. The true memory state is known after every turn. The store starts with 30 unrelated true \emph{background} memories and gains 10 between sessions, as months of earlier use would.

\subsection{Simulated Extractor and User}
The simulated extractor returns the operations a correct model would return, using only the candidates shown (a change whose target is not shown becomes an \textsf{add}, as a model would do). Errors are injected at rate $e$: a correct operation is dropped (\emph{miss}); a distractor becomes a false memory (\emph{spurious add}); a true memory shown to the model is retired or overwritten with a false value (\emph{wrong change}). Random draws are made in a fixed order per turn so that every policy faces the same errors. The simulated user reviews pending proposals at the end of each session, approves correct ones and rejects wrong ones, but errs with probability $u$.

\subsection{Policies}
\textbf{append}: only new facts are stored. \textbf{auto}: every operation is applied (AURA with the gate off). \textbf{gate}: changes wait for the user (AURA default). \textbf{gate-all}: additions are confirmed as well (emulated).

\subsection{Metrics}
Let $G$ be the set of true persona facts at the end and $A$ the active persona memories. Precision is $|A\cap G|/|A|$, recall $|A\cap G|/|G|$, and F1 their harmonic mean. We also report: \emph{stale} (active memories holding a value the user stated earlier but that is no longer true); \emph{false} (active memories the user never stated about themselves); and \emph{true facts destroyed}, the number of true memories, persona \emph{and background}, that ended superseded, outdated or deleted through a wrong change. F1 is blind to background memories, so destroyed facts is our safety metric. Burden is \emph{prompts per 100 turns} $=100\cdot(\text{review cards})/(\text{user turns})$, and \emph{prompt precision} is the share of cards that proposed a correct change. \emph{Reachability} is the share of change turns whose target memory is among the extractor's candidates. \emph{Forget residual} counts forget requests whose value remains in a memory row or in the conversation text. Means are reported with 95\% normal-approximation intervals over personas; proportions with Wilson intervals \cite{wilson1927}.

\subsection{Scoring a Real Extractor}
Gemini writes memories in its own words, so exact string matching fails. Memories are scored by the \emph{values} they mention: \emph{true}, \emph{ended} (a correct record that a retired fact ended), \emph{stale}, \emph{false}, \emph{hypothetical} (a hypothetical kept as a memory, counted as an error), \emph{third-party} (a fact about a person in the user's life, allowed), or \emph{other}. We check the scorer in two ways: against exact scoring on simulated output, and against human labels of a sample of memories, reporting Cohen's $\kappa$ \cite{cohen1960kappa} between the human and the automatic label.

\subsection{Reproducibility}
Simulated runs use a deterministic clock (one millisecond per call) because AURA orders memories by millisecond timestamps and same-millisecond ties otherwise cause run-to-run drift of about 0.5\%; a repeated slice matched the full run field by field. Runs are resumable and every run folder stores its configuration, raw rows and every final memory. The real extractor is \texttt{gemini-3.5-flash-lite}, AURA's default text model, run on \confirm{date of runs}.

\subsection{LongMemEval Setup (Experiment 5)}
We use the knowledge-update questions of LongMemEval \cite{wu2024longmemeval}. A full history has about 50 sessions, so each question is played with all its evidence sessions plus $k_d=3$ randomly chosen distractor sessions in date order (the same for every policy), with one extraction call per session. Answers are generated from the top-10 memories returned by AURA's search and graded by a Gemini judge following LongMemEval's knowledge-update rule and by string match. Two baselines bracket the policies: no memory, and the raw text of the same sessions in context. LongMemEval has no labels for which memory changes are correct, so the gate's reviewer is an \emph{oracle approximation}: it accepts proposals made while reading an evidence session and rejects the rest. Gate results on this benchmark are therefore an upper bracket on what a careful user could achieve, not a user measurement. In the \textbf{append} policy a changed fact is added next to the old one, as in append-only memory layers.

\section{Results}\label{sec:results}
All numbers are copied from the \texttt{summary.csv} files of the named run folders.

\subsection{Policies versus Extractor Error (RQ1)}
Table~\ref{tab:policy} and Fig.~\ref{fig:policies} compare the four policies for $e\in\{0,0.1,0.2,0.3\}$ with $u=0.05$ over \nn{} personas per cell.
With auto-apply, true facts destroyed grow with $e$; the gate reduces them by \nn\% at $e=0.2$. Most destroyed facts are background memories that F1 does not count, so F1 is nearly equal for auto and gate (\nn{} vs.\ \nn) while destroyed facts differ by an order of magnitude. The gate does not stop false \emph{new} facts (\nn{} false facts per persona vs.\ \nn{} under auto); only gate-all does, at about \nn$\times$ the prompts. Append-only destroys nothing but leaves \nn{} stale facts per persona even at $e=0$.

\noindent\textbf{User slips.}
Because a rejected proposal is never raised again, one mistaken rejection of a correct update keeps the old fact active for good. Table~\ref{tab:slip} varies $u$ at $e=0.1$: stale facts rise from \nn{} at $u=0$ to \nn{} at $u=0.3$, and prompt precision falls as $e$ grows (\nn{} at $e=0$ to \nn{} at $e=0.3$), so users see more wrong cards exactly when the gate matters most.

\subsection{Candidate Visibility and Retrieval (RQ2)}
The extractor can change only memories it is shown. Table~\ref{tab:reach} reports the share of change requests whose target is among the 20 candidates, for stores of $N$ unrelated memories and three phrasings of each change. For some phrasings a fact is not retrieved even in a small store (``I sold my old car and bought a Nexon'' does not retrieve ``The user drives a Swift''); when the target is missed, the old fact stays active next to the new one. Forget requests are affected most (\nn{} at $N=350$). Removing the minimum score from candidate selection (one environment variable) raises reachability to \nn{} at $N=350$ and, in Experiment 1, changes stale facts from \nn{} to \nn{} at $e=0.1$ under the gate (Fig.~\ref{fig:fix}). \confirm{direction of the change} The cost appears in retrieval: Fig.~\ref{fig:thresh} shows that the same threshold that hides targets also keeps never-stated questions from returning unrelated memories (noise \nn{} with it, \nn{} without), so the best setting differs for answering and for extraction.

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Discussion and Limitations}
\noindent\textbf{What the gate does and does not do.}
The gate prevents destructive changes but only those; false new facts pass unless additions are confirmed too, which multiplies the prompts. Two design consequences follow. First, report destroyed facts, not only F1, since background damage is invisible to accuracy. Second, a reject-forever rule protects against nagging but converts a user slip into a permanent stale fact; re-proposing after new evidence is a natural remedy that we did not evaluate.

\noindent\textbf{Candidate visibility is a precondition.}
A gate cannot approve a change the extractor is unable to propose. Candidate selection by similarity with a fixed minimum score hides targets that are worded differently from the new statement, and the fix is cheap but trades off against retrieval noise. Systems that separate ``find the memory to edit'' from ``find memories to answer with'' avoid the trade-off.

\noindent\textbf{Forgetting.}
Deleting a memory row leaves the conversation text it came from; whether that satisfies a user's request to forget depends on what the product promises, and MemCtrl \cite{memctrl2026} suggests that production systems often do not follow such requests.

\noindent\textbf{Limitations.}
(1) Experiments 1--3 use a simulated extractor whose errors are injected uniformly at rate $e$; real errors are likely correlated with the turn type. (2) Personas are scripted and synthetic. (3) The real-model samples are small and use one model, run on one date; hosted models change. (4) The user is simulated with a single slip rate, and there is no user study, so review burden and acceptance in practice are untested. (5) LongMemEval's gate uses an oracle reviewer and a Gemini judge, and we play a subset of each history. (6) Value-based scoring depends on hand-written value patterns; the human sample bounds but does not remove this. (7) Our related-work search was targeted rather than exhaustive.

%% ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Conclusion}
We measured an approval gate for model-edited long-term memory in a working assistant. The gate removes most destructive edits at a bounded prompt cost, fails to catch false additions, depends on the reviewing user, and cannot help when the extractor is not shown the memory to change. Making the target memory visible is a cheap and, in our measurements, effective complement. Future work includes a user study of review burden, re-proposal after new evidence, and evaluation with additional extractor models. Code, scenarios and all result files will be released at \confirm{repository URL}.

// Small helpers for 16 kHz mono PCM16 audio.
export const SAMPLE_RATE = 16000;

export function pcmToWav(pcm, sampleRate = SAMPLE_RATE) {
  const header = Buffer.alloc(44);
  header.write("RIFF", 0);
  header.writeUInt32LE(36 + pcm.length, 4);
  header.write("WAVE", 8);
  header.write("fmt ", 12);
  header.writeUInt32LE(16, 16);
  header.writeUInt16LE(1, 20); // PCM
  header.writeUInt16LE(1, 22); // mono
  header.writeUInt32LE(sampleRate, 24);
  header.writeUInt32LE(sampleRate * 2, 28);
  header.writeUInt16LE(2, 32);
  header.writeUInt16LE(16, 34);
  header.write("data", 36);
  header.writeUInt32LE(pcm.length, 40);
  return Buffer.concat([header, pcm]);
}

/** PCM16 little-endian buffer -> Float32Array in [-1, 1]. */
export function pcmToFloat32(pcm) {
  const n = Math.floor(pcm.length / 2);
  const out = new Float32Array(n);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out[i] = pcm.readInt16LE(i * 2) / 32768;
  return out;
}

export const pcmSeconds = (pcm) => pcm.length / 2 / SAMPLE_RATE;
